beats.text: In December 1912 Charles Dawson and Arthur Smith Woodward presented Piltdown Man to the Geological Society.
beats.note: It was billed as an early human ancestor.

beats.lead: Doubters spoke up almost at once
beats.text: Waterston in 1913 and Boule in 1915 argued it was an ape jaw with a human skull.
Tests in 1953 showed the jaw and teeth were not the same age as the skull, and the jaw was most likely an orangutan's.
beats.note: The skull was human and far more recent than claimed.

beats.context: From the 1912 announcement to the 1953 exposure.

beats.text: A 2016 study found one forger's methods throughout, and named Dawson.

beats.line: The fake survived because it said what experts wanted.
